data.text:
BARBERS RENEWS CALL FOR AI 'WATCHDOG' AMID RISE OF DEEPFAKES, DISINFORMATION

Surigao del Norte 2nd District Rep. Robert Ace Barbers on Wednesday renewed his call for the creation of a government "watchdog" to monitor and regulate the use and development of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in the Philippines, citing the growing threat posed by AI-generated deepfakes and online disinformation.

Barbers warned that the misuse of AI, particularly for spreading fake news, false narratives, and malicious propaganda, "poses a danger to society and humanity."

His call came after Sen. Bato Dela Rosa drew criticism for sharing an AI-generated video on social media featuring two students, believed to be Thai nationals, speaking in Tagalog in support of Vice President Sara Duterte amid her impeachment controversy.

"As I have said earlier, we should have a 'watchdog' to guard against unscrupulous individuals, like foreign propagandists, lobbyists, bandits or terrorist groups, that would take advantage of or use it for their selfish or criminal ends," Barbers said. "Mahirap yung patulog-tulog tayo sa pansitan sa mga bagay na ito."

The Mindanao lawmaker pushed for the revival and passage of pending measures, including his 2023 bill proposing the creation of the Artificial Intelligence Development Authority (AIDA), a superbody that would promote ethical AI development, ensure regulatory compliance, and protect public welfare.

"While the rapid phase of technological advancement in AI provides huge potential in the development of the people and the economy, it also poses risks and challenges that must be addressed to ensure that its benefits are maximized, and its negative impacts are minimized, if not avoided," Barbers said.

He emphasized that other countries, such as the U.S., U.K., European Union, and Singapore, have already taken steps to regulate AI, and the Philippines should not be left behind.

"Tulad ng paghahanda natin, kasama na ang pamahalaan, sa mga sakuna tulad ng bagyo, baha, lindol, sunog at iba pa, dapat din natin paghandaan ang daluyong na pwedeng dalhin sa ating bansa ng AI technology," he added. "Kasama na rin dito ang pagharap at pag-gamit nang kabutihang maidudulot nito sa ating lipunan, bansa at ekonomiya."

data.text:
Why China Is Dead Set on the South China Sea

China’s aggressive push in the West Philippine Sea may be driven by more than just oil, fishing grounds, or shipping lanes.

It's about energy dominance.

For years, analysts suspected vast methane hydrate deposits beneath our seabed: frozen methane trapped in ocean sediments or called "fire ice".  Methane hydrates can power China economy for more than 100 years and China has been quietly exploring  the area and investing in extraction technology, becoming one of only four countries capable of harvesting this powerful energy source. 

While China has been focused on extracting  fire ice from the seabed, a new and potentially even more valuable energy source has just been uncovered right on  our shores.

A recent study confirms that natural gas seeping from Nagsasa in San Antonio, Zambales, right along the country’s western corridor is now found to have the highest recorded content of naturally occurring hydrogen gas in the Philippines.  Known as geologic hydrogen, this natural source released a stunning 800 tons, far surpassing the previous global record of 200 tons in Albania just last year.

This renewable clean energy could power the entire town and signals massive potential for the Philippines in the global shift to green fuel.

Hydrogen is the fuel of the future.  It's cleaner than methane, zero carbon emissions, and highly valuable in the global energy transition.

Put the pieces together:
-Methane hydrate in the deep waters.
-Natural hydrogen from ultramafic rocks in Zambales.
-A tectonic zone rich in resources the world is now racing to control.

China’s aim isn’t just to claim the sea, but to corner the future of energy.  And it won’t stop with the Philippines. If left unchecked, every nation bordering the South China Sea may one day face the same fate, cut off from their own resources, their sovereignty slowly eroded, their future bargained away.
